title: Inherited constructible triangles and exact ambient scalar extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $X$ be a scheme with Noetherian underlying space, and let $E$ be a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. Use $E_X=p_X^*C(-,E)$ with its restricted norm topology and $\Omega_X=p_X^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions valued in one finite intermediate field [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Let $\mathcal C_E=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{E_X})$ with bounded stratified locally finitely presented cohomology, and let $\iota_E$ be its full inclusion [def-sfb-dcons-subfield, sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

The category $\mathcal C_E$ has the inherited pretriangulated structure, its integer shift functors are additive, and $\iota_E$ is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For the coefficient inclusion $E_X\to\Omega_X$ [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map], the ordinary scalar-extension functor $F_E=\Omega_X\otimes_{E_X}-$ between the abelian internal module categories is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Its derived extension $T_{E,\Omega}=LF_E$ [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar] is canonically identified with $D(F_E)$, the functor applying $F_E$ termwise to a representing complex [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. With the integer-shift comparison transported through this canonical identification, $T_{E,\Omega}$ is triangulated. In particular $T_{E,\Omega}\iota_E$ is triangulated and is canonically identified, compatibly with shifts, with the restriction of exact termwise scalar extension. No triangulated structure on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Omega)$ is required.

proof.text: Work in the fixed coefficient universe and the small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ from [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Ab}$: the ambient category $\mathcal S=\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathrm{Ab})$ is abelian, symmetric monoidal closed, and has additive tensor product preserving colimits separately. In particular both $E_X\otimes-$ and $\Omega_X\otimes-$ preserve finite colimits. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] to each of the two commutative coefficient ring objects to obtain the abelian categories $\mathcal A_E=\operatorname{Mod}_{E_X}$ and $\mathcal A_\Omega=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Omega_X}$. The hypotheses of clause 2 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] hold in $\mathcal S$: coequalizers exist, the tensor product preserves colimits in both variables, and $E_X$ is commutative. Thus its extension along $E_X\to\Omega_X$ is precisely $F_E$ and preserves finite colimits, including the initial object.

source.place: Complexes paragraph, ambient module categories and ordinary scalar extension; sheaf and module-category hypotheses expanded

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B_E$ be the strictly full class of constructible objects in $\mathcal A_E$. The finite-field case of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre] applies with $T=X$: it assumes only that the underlying space is Noetherian. Its coefficient ring $E_X^c$ and its stratified local finite-presentation predicate are those of the archived construction of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre]; [lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-presentation-identification] identifies $E_X^c$ with our $E_X$, compatibly with units and multiplication (hence the internal module categories), and identifies that predicate with the constructibility of [def-sfb-constructible-module] used in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with the same strata and presentations. Transported through this identification, it gives closure under kernels and cokernels of maps between members and under extensions. The zero module belongs to $\mathcal B_E$: on the single stratum $X$ it has the presentation $E_X^0\to E_X^0\to0$, using the identity cover. This remains valid for empty $X$. An isomorphism transports the same local presentations, so $\mathcal B_E$ is strictly full. Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to $\mathcal A_E$ and $\mathcal B_E$, using its bounded version. It makes the full subcategory of objects with bounded constructible cohomology a triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal A_E)$. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and [def-sfb-dcons-subfield], this is exactly $\mathcal C_E$, with no completeness or étale-origin restriction.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including bounded versions; coefficient-specific closure is the cited condensed-field node

proof.text: By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], the subcategory just obtained carries the inherited pretriangulated structure and its inclusion $\iota_E$ is triangulated. Here a triangle is distinguished precisely when its image under $\iota_E$ is distinguished. Integer shifts are the restrictions of the ambient shifts of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hom groups and their addition are unchanged by the full inclusion. Thus for morphisms $f,g$ in $\mathcal C_E$ the equality $(f+g)[n]=f[n]+g[n]$ is the corresponding ambient equality; the ambient shifts are additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category] (integer shifts are powers of the additive shift equivalence). Hence every integer shift on $\mathcal C_E$ is additive.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: bounded constructible complexes form a triangulated subcategory; inherited shifts and full inclusion made explicit

proof.text: The flatness statement [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat] applies to the same inclusion $E_X\to\Omega_X$, for this finite field $E$ and arbitrary scheme $X$, and gives preservation of finite limits by $F_E$. Together with step 1 this gives preservation of finite limits and finite colimits. For additivity, identify $F_E(M\oplus N)$ with $F_E(M)\oplus F_E(N)$ by its preserved binary product and coproduct diagrams. This comparison takes the two projections and the two inclusions to the corresponding projections and inclusions, since $F_E$ preserves zero objects and hence zero morphisms. It therefore takes the diagonal $\Delta_M$, the codiagonal $\nabla_N$, and $f\oplus g$ to their counterparts. Applying $F_E$ to $f+g=\nabla_N\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta_M$ gives $F_E(f+g)=F_E(f)+F_E(g)$. Also $F_E(0)=0$. Thus $F_E$ is an exact additive functor between the two abelian categories.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: exactness from lem-sfb-qlbar-flat; finite-colimit and additivity clauses expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $F_E$, with exactness and additivity established in step 4. It supplies a triangulated functor $G=D(F_E):D(\mathcal A_E)\to D(\mathcal A_\Omega)$ and a natural factorization isomorphism $\varphi_K:G(Q_EK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_\Omega(C(F_E)K)$ compatible with every integer shift. In particular any representing complex is sent termwise, with no resolution required. On complexes the shift comparison is the identity in each degree: the two differentials agree because $F_E((-1)^n d)=(-1)^nF_E(d)$. The cited theorem includes the descent of this comparison and its compatibility with $\varphi$, so no assertion of shift compatibility is being inferred merely from the existence of an unstructured factorization isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; exact termwise factorization with shifts as in Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.lean, lines 35–105

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], the pair $(G,\varphi)$ of step 5 is itself a total left derived functor. By [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], $T=T_{E,\Omega}$ is the total left derived extension of this same ordinary $F_E$. The total left derived functor of [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar] is taken along $K(\mathcal A_E)\to D(\mathcal A_E)$, the cited one along $Q_E:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A_E)\to D(\mathcal A_E)$; since $Q_E$ is the composite with the quotient $\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A_E)\to K(\mathcal A_E)$, which is a localization (bijective on objects and full), precomposition with it is fully faithful on functor categories, and the termwise functor $Q_\Omega C(F_E)$ factors through it because the additive $F_E$ preserves homotopies; so the two right Kan extension properties are the same. Consequently their universal properties give canonical comparison maps $a:T\to G$ and $b:G\to T$ respecting their counits. The composites $ba$ and $ab$ respect the respective counits too; uniqueness in each universal property identifies them with the identities. Thus $a:T\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ is the canonical derived comparison. This proves the comparison with termwise extension without using extra existence hypotheses on K-flat resolutions. It is the canonical exact-functor comparison described in the statement.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and its left-derived dual; uniqueness of the universal comparison written out

proof.text:
Write $\sigma^G_{K,n}:G(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K)[n]$ for the comparisons of step 5. Give $T$ the transported comparisons
$$\sigma^T_{K,n}=(a_K[n])^{-1}\circ\sigma^G_{K,n}\circ a_{K[n]}.$$
Naturality follows by substituting the naturality identities for $a$ and $\sigma^G$; the shift-unit and shift-composition identities follow from those for $G$ by cancellation of adjacent $a$ and $a^{-1}$. For a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\xrightarrow{w}K[1]$, its images under $T$ and $G$ are isomorphic by $(a_K,a_L,a_M)$. Naturality gives the first two triangle squares. For the last square the formula gives
$$a_K[1]\circ\sigma^T_{K,1}\circ T(w)=\sigma^G_{K,1}\circ G(w)\circ a_M.$$
The $G$-image is distinguished, so the $T$-image is distinguished by isomorphism invariance in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Additivity transfers through $a$ by the same naturality equations on Hom groups. Thus $T$ is triangulated with precisely the comparison specified in the item.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: exact scalar extension carries the cone triangle to the ambient distinguished triangle; transported integer-shift comparison expanded

proof.text: The composite $T\circ\iota_E$ is additive. Its shift comparison is the composite $T(\iota_E(K[n]))\cong T((\iota_EK)[n])\xrightarrow{\sigma^T}T(\iota_EK)[n]$. A distinguished triangle of $\mathcal C_E$ first becomes distinguished under $\iota_E$ by step 3 and then under $T$ by step 7. Thus the composite is triangulated by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Whiskering $a$ by $\iota_E$ identifies it with $G\circ\iota_E$; the formula in step 7 says exactly that this identification respects all shifts. By step 5 the latter functor is the restriction of exact termwise scalar extension. All image triangles lie in $D(\mathcal A_\Omega)$, which completes every assertion without requiring any triangle structure on a constructible subcategory over $\Omega$.
